title: Leveraging UAV and Satellite Imagery for Precision Agricultural Mapping and Extension Services
content: The Enabling Crop Analytics at scale (ECAAS) project aims to produce open-access agricultural maps and ground truth data to improve the delivery of farm extension services. In order to provide farm extension services more effectively, the ECAAS project is focused on producing open-access agricultural maps and ground truth data. High-resolution maps of crop varieties and the potential yields associated with them will be made using this data. These maps will be used to locate possible production improvement regions and to give farmers more precise and timely information. The project will also track crop health and spot regions of crop stress using satellite imagery and ground-based data. Delivering efficient farm extension services necessitates the creation of open-access agricultural maps and ground truth data. Farmers can obtain information about their land and the resources at their disposal by the created precise and current maps of agricultural land. To better understand the demands of farmers and determine how to best meet those needs, ground truth data, such as crop yields and soil types, can also be employed. Farm extension services can be tailored to the particular needs of individual farmers and offer them the greatest support by using open-access agricultural maps and ground truth data. Ground truth data and open-access agricultural maps are key tools for providing farm extension services more effectively. We can provide a complete description of the land, including its topography, vegetation, and soil type, by developing open access agricultural maps. Using this information, farm extension services such as crop advisories, pest control programs, and soil conservation techniques can be developed that are more precise and efficient. For the purpose of providing reliable data about the land and its resources, ground truth data is equally crucial. We can improve our understanding of the current state of the land and its resources and create more valuable farm extension services by gathering and evaluating such data. We can provide farmers with more precise and efficient farm extension services by developing open-access agricultural maps and gathering real-world data.
